pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as a two-part answer to his specific problem — mobility to correct the compensations, kettlebells to build the mass — and he bought the logic completely: 'your program sounds way better than Kettlebell Grants for what I want to do.' He had arrived pre-sold on the modality on his own theory that twisting movements unwind the fascial system, and he engaged actively with the rep's before-and-after alignment photos: 'you're more in your lower body and in your midsection. You drop down, your embodiment is much lower.'

Deliberately deprioritised by the rep rather than presented: 'we have our own nutrition side of things. Now you, it sounds like you have that. So that would be way less of a priority than the other two things', and later 'it sounds like nutritionally for you, it's a lot deeper than hitting micronutrients and hitting macros... we can still lend an ear if we need to, to optimize.' The prospect accepted this readily — 'the guy I work with, he's a fitness nut too, on nutrition and understanding my body's chemistry.' A defensible call given he is on a clinician-prescribed protocol, but it means one of the three pillars was surrendered before it was sold.

24/7 access to Trevor, the True Coach app and the weekly check-in were all presented. The prospect's only response was a mechanics question — 'Is that like Slack or WhatsApp or what is that word?' — with no engagement with the accountability value itself. Notable given that his stated failure mode is a crash cycle that would need close weekly monitoring.

anchors.raw: I just spent... I spent... spent... Um, 50-some K on another coaching package for my business. So, uh, and, but I'm, but I didn't, but I pulled that out of the business. I got my own personal savings I could just pull it out of.
anchors.note: The strongest price-supporting anchor in the batch. A recent fifty-thousand-dollar coaching purchase makes $6,000 roughly twelve per cent of his established coaching spend, and he separately confirmed personal savings he could draw on. Price was never a live issue on this call, which is exactly why the rep's unprompted offer to break the payment up was a mistake.

anchors.raw: That's, that there's that other kettlebell guy. He charges the exact same amount. Um, kettlebell grant.
anchors.note: A directly comparable named competitor at exact price parity, which validates $6,000 as the market rate rather than undercutting it. The prospect then differentiated in Primal's favour on two grounds — that Grant assigns you to a coach rather than the principal, and that Grant's positioning is leanness rather than hypertrophy. Worth noting the competitor bundles hardware the offer does not: 'he does send you a Hume scale, and he does send you kettlebells.'

anchors.raw: I had looked at functional patterns, actually. I thought that would help me with my alignment, but the guys with functional patterns were just, the guy I was working with online just didn't, he was really hard to schedule with and didn't show up. And I got tired of the arrogant energy from those guys.
anchors.note: He has already paid for online alignment coaching and it failed him on service rather than on price — unreliable scheduling, no-shows, and an attitude he found intolerable. That sets a low bar to beat on delivery and removes price as the comparison axis entirely. He also pays a functional medicine practitioner in Australia, so paying experts for health is an established habit.

unmet_demand.want: Training programmed around an autoimmune crash threshold — 'I'm worried about how much I can push it without getting a cytokine response'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing in the offer describes how load is titrated for an autoimmune patient, who monitors for a crash, or what happens to a six-month programme when a crash costs a week. The rep's only substantive assurance was an unqualified claim that 'the mobility stuff, it doesn't tax a CNS', and the weekly check-in was presented as a progression tool rather than a safety mechanism. Whether the programme can safely serve this physiology is not established on this call and needs a human to decide.

unmet_demand.want: Targeted correction of specific structural presentations — distended lower abdomen, anterior pelvic tilt, rib flare, mild pectus excavatum and mild scoliosis. He asked directly: 'can we specifically focus on these misalignments and do stuff to specifically get [them], or is it just the exercise alone will do it for me?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered that the mobility work addresses it and that the process starts with watching him move on video. That may be true for the soft-tissue and activation components, but pectus excavatum and scoliosis are skeletal, and no boundary was drawn between what remote coaching can influence and what it cannot. The prospect's expectation, formed partly from a ChatGPT assessment that 'with some really good training, you should be able to work that out', went unqualified.

unmet_demand.want: Training delivered as emotional embodiment work — lifting performed with the intention of releasing stored trauma, which is his own professional method
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme has no such component and the rep had never encountered the idea: 'Interesting. I've never heard that one before' and 'Makes sense, actually. I'm going to look into that.' The prospect explicitly wants the invoice framed as 'some form of embodiment program' because 'that's pretty much what it is anyways' to him — so he is buying against an expectation the product does not describe or deliver.
